title: Prove Settings-denied workspace reads never invoke the read module
goal: Add a canonical M8 integration regression proving the Settings-backed read capability is enforced before the workspace read module runs.
context: Issue #347 requires Settings capability toggles to be honored by the production runtime. Write denial and global workspace-tools denial already have no-invocation coverage; the equivalent read-capability boundary needs a direct regression.
forbidden_changes: Do not change production execution behavior or grant capabilities.
Do not weaken policy, Agent scope, approval, schema validation, cancellation, workspace path/protected-file checks, secret scanning, size limits, or verification.
Do not treat an unchanged file alone as proof that no read capability execution occurred.
Do not claim physical-device acceptance from CI.
acceptance_criteria: With the Settings-backed read capability disabled, the canonical M8 read request is denied.
The denied request emits no moduleInvoked event for tool.workspace.read.
The denied request emits no successful or verified observation for workspace.read-file.
The fixture remains intact and existing positive read-path regressions remain unchanged.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
recovery: If the regression exposes a production bypass, stop and investigate the Module policy boundary rather than weakening the assertion. If a required gate fails, repair only within allowed_paths or revert this logical task; never bypass policy or claim device acceptance.
